mustKnow.source: NICE diabetes in pregnancy; ADA Standards of Care 2025

mustKnow.fact: ADA glucose targets in pregnancy are a fasting glucose below 95 mg/dL, a 1-hour postmeal glucose below 140 mg/dL, and a 2-hour postmeal glucose below 120 mg/dL. NICE uses slightly different self-monitoring targets. Insulin is adjusted to the targets the chosen guideline sets, not to a nonpregnant HbA1c of 7%.

Pregestational diabetes needs contraception until the HbA1c is as close to 6.5% as is safe, high-dose folate, and stop of ACE inhibitors, ARBs, and statins before conception. First-trimester hyperglycemia causes congenital malformations, classically caudal regression, cardiac defects, and neural tube defects.

Poor glucose control later in pregnancy causes macrosomia, shoulder dystocia, neonatal hypoglycemia, polycythemia, and hypocalcemia. A normal delivery does not cancel the need for a neonatal glucose check.

Women with gestational diabetes have a 75 g OGTT at 4 to 12 weeks after delivery to reclassify them. Many have persistent dysglycemia. They also have a high lifetime risk of type 2 diabetes and need ongoing screening.

CONCEPTT showed that continuous glucose monitoring in pregnant women with type 1 diabetes improved neonatal outcomes compared with capillary monitoring. It does not replace the preconception HbA1c target.

topics.title: Monogenic and secondary diabetes
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 37 Monogenic Diabetes

mustKnow.fact: Suspect monogenic diabetes when diabetes presents before 6 months of age, when a young lean adult has a strong autosomal dominant family history and negative islet antibodies, or when diabetes travels with renal cysts, deafness, or a syndromic picture. Do not label every antibody-negative young adult as type 2 diabetes.
mustKnow.source: ADA Standards of Care 2025; Williams Endocrinology 15e Ch. 37

mustKnow.fact: GCK-MODY causes stable mild fasting hyperglycemia, often 100 to 144 mg/dL, that does not progress like type 2 diabetes and usually needs no treatment outside pregnancy. HbA1c sits near the top of the nondiabetic range for life.

HNF1A-MODY is sensitive to low-dose sulfonylurea, which is first-line drug therapy, and it progresses, unlike GCK-MODY. HNF4A-MODY is similar and also causes fetal macrosomia and neonatal hypoglycemia. HNF1B disease combines diabetes with renal cysts, genital malformations, and hypomagnesemia.

Neonatal diabetes diagnosed before 6 months is often a KCNJ11 or ABCC8 variant in the KATP channel. Many of these infants can be transferred from insulin to a sulfonylurea. Diabetes after 6 to 12 months is much more often type 1.

Maternally inherited diabetes and deafness is the m.3243A>G mitochondrial variant. Metformin is used cautiously because of the lactic acidosis risk in mitochondrial disease. Inheritance is maternal, so an affected father does not transmit it.
Wolfram syndrome, DIDMOAD, is diabetes insipidus, diabetes mellitus, optic atrophy, and deafness, from WFS1. Optic atrophy in a child with diabetes is not ordinary retinopathy.

Generalized lipodystrophy causes severe insulin resistance, low leptin, and hypertriglyceridemia. Metreleptin is replacement for generalized lipodystrophy. Finding almost no subcutaneous fat changes the treatment from ordinary type 2 diabetes drugs.

New diabetes in an older thin adult can be the first sign of pancreatic cancer. Steroid hyperglycemia and post-transplant diabetes are secondary. Cystic fibrosis-related diabetes is treated with insulin, and screening uses an annual OGTT from about age 10, not HbA1c alone.

topics.title: Obesity and metabolic syndrome
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 40 Obesity and Neuroendocrine Control of Energy Stores

mustKnow.fact: WHO body-mass index cutoffs are 25 kg/m2 for overweight and 30 kg/m2 for obesity. For Asian-Indian adults the consensus cutoffs are lower: overweight at 23 kg/m2 and obesity at 25 kg/m2, because metabolic risk appears at a lower BMI.

A practical metabolic syndrome definition needs three of five: a large waist (Indian cutoffs often 90 cm in men and 80 cm in women), triglycerides of 150 mg/dL or higher, HDL cholesterol below 40 mg/dL in men or below 50 mg/dL in women, blood pressure of 130/85 mmHg or higher, and fasting glucose of 100 mg/dL or higher.
mustKnow.source: ATP III metabolic syndrome criteria with Indian waist cutoffs

mustKnow.fact: Leptin deficiency causes severe early obesity with hypogonadotropic hypogonadism and is treated with leptin. MC4R variants are the commonest monogenic obesity. Setmelanotide is used for selected pathway defects including POMC, PCSK1, and LEPR deficiency, not for ordinary polygenic obesity.

Prader-Willi syndrome causes neonatal hypotonia and then hyperphagia, hypogonadism, and short stature from loss of paternally expressed genes on 15q11. Growth hormone is used in childhood. Uncontrolled food access, not a lack of willpower, drives the weight.

Semaglutide 2.4 mg weekly, studied in the STEP trials, and tirzepatide, studied in the SURMOUNT trials, produce large mean weight loss in obesity and are used with diet, not instead of a food plan. Orlistat blocks fat absorption and can cause deficiency of fat-soluble vitamins.

Bariatric surgery is considered at a BMI of 40 kg/m2 or higher, or 35 kg/m2 or higher with a serious comorbidity such as type 2 diabetes. Asian-Indian guidance uses lower thresholds, often a BMI of 32.5 kg/m2 with comorbidity. It is the most effective treatment for severe obesity and can remit type 2 diabetes.

Roux-en-Y gastric bypass causes more micronutrient deficiency than sleeve gastrectomy, especially iron, vitamin B12, vitamin D, calcium, and thiamine. Thiamine deficiency can present as Wernicke encephalopathy after prolonged vomiting. Supplement and monitor for life, not for one year.

Dumping syndrome and post-bariatric hypoglycemia are late effects of bypass. Diet is the first treatment. A patient who is losing weight too fast with vomiting needs thiamine before dextrose is given alone.

topics.title: Dyslipidaemia
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 41 Disorders of Lipoprotein Metabolism; ESC dyslipidemia guideline 2019

mustKnow.fact: For very high cardiovascular risk, the ESC LDL cholesterol goal is below 55 mg/dL and at least a 50% reduction from baseline. Many ACC pathways still use below 70 mg/dL for high-risk patients. State which guideline you are applying when you quote a target.
mustKnow.source: ESC dyslipidemia guideline 2019; ACC cholesterol pathway

mustKnow.fact: Suspect familial hypercholesterolemia when adult LDL cholesterol is above 190 mg/dL, when tendon xanthomas are present, or when premature coronary disease runs in the family. The Dutch Lipid Clinic Network score formalizes that suspicion. The common genes are LDLR, APOB, and gain-of-function PCSK9.

High-intensity statins are atorvastatin 40 to 80 mg or rosuvastatin 20 to 40 mg. Check creatine kinase if the patient has muscle symptoms. Stop the statin if creatine kinase is above 10 times the upper limit. Do not combine gemfibrozil with a statin; if a fibrate is required, use fenofibrate.
mustKnow.source: ACC/AHA cholesterol guideline; Williams Endocrinology 15e Ch. 41

mustKnow.fact: Homozygous familial hypercholesterolemia presents in childhood with LDL cholesterol often above 400 mg/dL and can cause supravalvular aortic stenosis. Treatment adds ezetimibe, a PCSK9 inhibitor, and when needed evinacumab, lomitapide, or lipoprotein apheresis.

Triglycerides above 500 mg/dL are treated to reduce pancreatitis risk, and risk is high above 1000 mg/dL. Eruptive xanthomas and lipemia retinalis are the clinical clues. Fenofibrate, not a statin, is the drug aimed at very high triglycerides. Icosapent ethyl reduced cardiovascular events in REDUCE-IT in statin-treated patients with triglycerides that were raised but below the pancreatitis range.

Familial chylomicronemia from lipoprotein lipase or APOC2 deficiency causes recurrent pancreatitis with triglycerides in the thousands and a creamy supernatant. Volanesorsen and olezarsen lower apoC-III. A very low-fat diet is still required.

Dysbetalipoproteinemia, type III, is usually APOE2 homozygosity. Cholesterol and triglycerides are both high, and palmar xanthomas are characteristic. It responds well to a fibrate and to treatment of coexisting diabetes or hypothyroidism.

Measure lipoprotein(a) once in a lifetime in a person with premature cardiovascular disease or familial hypercholesterolemia. A value above about 50 mg/dL is a risk enhancer. Statins do not lower it meaningfully. PCSK9 inhibitors lower it modestly. Niacin is not used for outcome benefit after AIM-HIGH and HPS2-THRIVE.

topics.title: Male hypogonadism and gynaecomastia
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 17 Testicular Disorders; Endocrine Society testosterone therapy guideline 2018

mustKnow.fact: Diagnose hypogonadism with two morning fasting total testosterone measurements, ideally before 10 am, and then measure LH and FSH. A single afternoon level is not enough. If the total testosterone is borderline and SHBG is likely abnormal, measure free testosterone.

Primary hypogonadism has a high LH. Klinefelter syndrome, 47,XXY, is the common genetic cause: small firm testes, azoospermia, tall stature, and gynecomastia. Secondary hypogonadism has a low or inappropriately normal LH. Kallmann syndrome adds anosmia because GnRH neurons fail to migrate.

Testosterone therapy is for men with symptoms and consistently low testosterone. It suppresses spermatogenesis, so it is the wrong drug when fertility is the goal. Use hCG, and add FSH if spermatogenesis does not start, when the couple wants a pregnancy.

Do not start testosterone in prostate cancer, male breast cancer, a hematocrit that is already high, or untreated severe obstructive sleep apnea, or when a baby is planned in the near term. Recheck hematocrit, because erythrocytosis is the common adverse effect.

The TRAVERSE trial found that testosterone gel was noninferior to placebo for major adverse cardiovascular events in middle-aged and older hypogonadal men with cardiovascular risk. That does not make testosterone a treatment for aging in a man with a normal testosterone.

Anabolic steroid misuse suppresses LH and FSH, shrinks the testes, lowers HDL cholesterol, and raises hematocrit. Infertility can persist for months after the drugs are stopped. The testosterone may be high or low depending on the timing of the last injection.

Gynecomastia is glandular breast tissue in a man. Physiologic puberty, spironolactone, ketoconazole, cirrhosis, hyperthyroidism, prolactin excess, and Klinefelter syndrome are the usual causes. A hard eccentric mass, skin tethering, or bloody nipple discharge needs exclusion of breast cancer.
Obesity lowers SHBG, so total testosterone falls while free testosterone may be normal. Weight loss is the first treatment of that pattern. Testosterone is not a weight-loss drug for a eugonadal man.

modules.name: PCOS, amenorrhoea and female reproductive endocrinology

topics.title: PCOS, amenorrhoea and female reproductive endocrinology
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 15 Physiology and Pathology of the Female Reproductive Axis; international PCOS guideline 2018 and 2023

mustKnow.fact: Secondary amenorrhea is no menses for 3 months if cycles were regular, or 6 months if they were irregular. The first tests are pregnancy, TSH, prolactin, and FSH. Do not order a pelvic ultrasound before pregnancy is excluded.

Rotterdam polycystic ovary syndrome needs 2 of 3 features: oligo-ovulation or anovulation, clinical or biochemical hyperandrogenism, and polycystic ovarian morphology, after other causes are excluded. Using a modern transducer, morphology is 20 or more follicles in either ovary or a volume of 10 mL or more. Older criteria used 12 follicles. The LH to FSH ratio is not a diagnostic criterion.

Hirsutism is usually a modified Ferriman-Gallwey score of 8 or higher, with a lower cutoff in some East Asian populations. Combined oral contraceptives are first-line drug therapy. Spironolactone is antiandrogenic and teratogenic, so contraception is required. Letrozole, not clomiphene, is first-line ovulation induction.

Functional hypothalamic amenorrhea is low GnRH drive from energy deficit, low LH, and low estradiol. The treatment is to eat more and train less. An oral contraceptive does not protect bone as well as restoring endogenous estrogen, and it hides whether recovery has occurred.
mustKnow.source: Endocrine Society functional hypothalamic amenorrhea guideline

mustKnow.fact: Premature ovarian insufficiency is amenorrhea before 40 years with two FSH values in the menopausal range, at least a month apart. Give hormone therapy until the average age of natural menopause unless there is a contraindication. Causes include Turner syndrome, an FMR1 premutation, autoimmune disease, and iatrogenic injury.

Turner syndrome, 45,X, causes short stature, streak gonads, coarctation of the aorta, bicuspid aortic valve, horseshoe kidney, and autoimmune thyroid disease. Pregnancy, if ever achieved, carries a high risk of aortic dissection and needs specialist care.

Offer menopausal hormone therapy for bothersome vasomotor symptoms to a woman younger than 60 years or within 10 years of menopause who has no contraindication. The Women's Health Initiative found that combined estrogen plus progestin increased breast cancer, stroke, and venous thromboembolism and reduced fractures. Do not start hormone therapy to prevent cardiovascular disease. Transdermal estrogen has a lower clot risk than oral estrogen.

Rapid virilization with a testosterone often above 150 to 200 ng/dL suggests an androgen-secreting tumor rather than polycystic ovary syndrome. A high DHEAS points toward an adrenal source. Image after the biochemistry, not before.

topics.title: Disorders of puberty
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 23 Physiology and Disorders of Puberty

mustKnow.fact: Central precocious puberty is GnRH-dependent. The traditional age cutoffs are breast development before 8 years in a girl and testicular enlargement before 9 years in a boy. A GnRH stimulation test shows a pubertal LH response. Treatment is a long-acting GnRH agonist.

Peripheral precocious puberty is GnRH-independent, with suppressed LH and high sex steroids. Causes include McCune-Albright syndrome, an activating LH-receptor variant (familial male-limited precocious puberty), congenital adrenal hyperplasia, a sex-steroid tumor, and exogenous hormone.

McCune-Albright syndrome combines cafe-au-lait macules with a coast-of-Maine border, fibrous dysplasia, and recurrent estrogen production from an activating GNAS variant. GnRH agonist therapy does not stop the peripheral sex-steroid production.

Constitutional delay of growth and puberty is the commonest cause of late puberty, especially in boys. There is a family history, bone age is delayed, and adult height lands in the family range. It is a diagnosis made while hypogonadotropic hypogonadism is still possible.

Delayed puberty is no breast development by 13 years in a girl, or testicular volume still below 4 mL by 14 years in a boy. The first tests are bone age, LH, FSH, and the appropriate sex steroid, plus TSH and prolactin if the history suggests a sellar mass.

Kallmann syndrome is hypogonadotropic hypogonadism with anosmia. A normal sense of smell does not exclude other genetic hypogonadotropic hypogonadism. Inhibin B and AMH help separate a constitutional delay, where Sertoli cell markers are more preserved, from true deficiency.

Isolated premature thelarche and isolated premature adrenarche are usually benign if growth velocity and the rest of puberty are normal. Progressive breast development with a growth spurt is central precocious puberty until the GnRH test says otherwise.

Loss-of-function variants in the paternally expressed gene MKRN3 cause familial central precocious puberty. Kisspeptin stimulates GnRH and is the pathway those variants disturb. A family history of early puberty in a parent is a clue.

topics.title: Differences of sex development
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 21 Differences of Sex Development

mustKnow.fact: A virilized or ambiguous newborn needs an urgent karyotype, serum electrolytes, and 17-hydroxyprogesterone. Salt-wasting 21-hydroxylase deficiency can cause hyponatremia, hyperkalemia, and shock in the first 1 to 4 weeks of life.
The commonest 46,XX difference of sex development is virilizing congenital adrenal hyperplasia. A uterus is present because there was no anti-Mullerian hormone. Androgen exposure was prenatal.

Complete androgen insensitivity is a 46,XY difference. Testes produce anti-Mullerian hormone, so the uterus is absent, and testosterone is high but the receptor does not respond. At puberty there is breast development from aromatized androgen, a blind vaginal pouch, and sparse pubic hair.

5-alpha-reductase deficiency raises the testosterone to dihydrotestosterone ratio. A 46,XY infant may look undervirilized and then virilize at puberty when testosterone rises. Breast development does not occur, which separates it from complete androgen insensitivity.

17-beta-hydroxysteroid dehydrogenase type 3 deficiency also undervirilizes a 46,XY fetus. Androstenedione is high and testosterone is low, the opposite pattern of the ratio used in 5-alpha-reductase deficiency.

Sertoli cells make anti-Mullerian hormone, which regresses the Mullerian ducts. Leydig cells make testosterone, which stabilizes the Wolffian ducts. Absence of a uterus means functional Sertoli cells were present in fetal life, even if the external genitalia look female.

A dysgenetic gonad that contains Y material has a risk of gonadoblastoma. Gonadectomy is individualized. In complete androgen insensitivity the gonads are often left in place through puberty so spontaneous breast development can occur, and the malignancy risk is then reassessed.

Sex assignment is a multidisciplinary decision that uses karyotype, gonadal function, anatomy, and the family's informed choice. Phallus size alone does not decide it, and elective cosmetic surgery in infancy is not an emergency.

modules.name: Growth disorders and growth hormone therapy

topics.title: Growth disorders and growth hormone therapy
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 22 Normal and Aberrant Growth in Children; Ch. 6 Pituitary Physiology and Diagnostic Evaluation

mustKnow.fact: Before any stimulation test, measure height accurately, plot growth velocity, calculate mid-parental height, and obtain a bone age. A short child who is growing at a normal velocity along a centile close to the mid-parental height usually has familial short stature, not growth hormone deficiency.

An IGF-1 that is normal for age and pubertal stage makes severe growth hormone deficiency unlikely. A low IGF-1 supports the diagnosis but is not sufficient, because malnutrition, hypothyroidism, and chronic illness also lower it.

Isolated growth hormone deficiency is usually confirmed with two stimulation tests, because a single test has a high false-positive rate. A traditional peak below 10 mcg/L supports deficiency. Many current assays use a lower cutoff, so the laboratory method is part of the result.

In adults, the insulin tolerance test remains the reference test when it is safe. A peak growth hormone at or below 5.1 mcg/L supports deficiency on the Endocrine Society criterion. It is contraindicated in ischemic heart disease and seizure disorder.
mustKnow.source: Endocrine Society evaluation of adult growth hormone deficiency

mustKnow.fact: Laron syndrome is growth hormone receptor resistance. Growth hormone is high, IGF-1 is very low, and growth hormone treatment does not work. Recombinant IGF-1, mecasermin, is the replacement.

Growth hormone is approved without classic deficiency for Turner syndrome, SHOX deficiency, small-for-gestational-age children who have not caught up by about 2 to 4 years of age, Prader-Willi syndrome, and growth failure of chronic kidney disease. The indication is the syndrome, not a failed stimulation test.

Counsel families that growth hormone can cause benign intracranial hypertension, slipped capital femoral epiphysis, worsening of scoliosis, and insulin resistance. A limp or severe headache on treatment is not a routine growing pain.

Achondroplasia is an FGFR3 gain of function and is not treated as growth hormone deficiency. Vosoritide, a C-type natriuretic peptide analogue, is the disease-modifying drug. Vosoritide is not a treatment for idiopathic short stature.

modules.name: Multiple endocrine neoplasia and hereditary endocrine tumours

topics.title: Multiple endocrine neoplasia and hereditary endocrine tumours
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 42 Endocrine Neoplasia Syndromes

mustKnow.fact: MEN1, from menin on 11q, is parathyroid adenoma or hyperplasia in over 90% of patients, plus pituitary adenoma (often prolactinoma) and enteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumors (gastrinoma more often than insulinoma). Onset of hyperparathyroidism is usually in the teens or twenties. Surgery for the parathyroids addresses multigland disease, not a single adenoma assumed in sporadic disease.

MEN2A is RET activation with medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, and hyperparathyroidism. MEN2B is medullary thyroid carcinoma, pheochromocytoma, mucosal neuromas, a marfanoid habitus, and intestinal ganglioneuromatosis, without hyperparathyroidism. The common MEN2B variant is RET M918T.
mustKnow.source: ATA medullary thyroid cancer guidance; Williams Endocrinology 15e Ch. 42

mustKnow.fact: Prophylactic thyroidectomy in MEN2 is timed by the RET codon risk. MEN2B with M918T is operated in the first year of life. In MEN2A the age depends on the codon. Screen for pheochromocytoma with metanephrines and treat it before any thyroidectomy.
MEN4, from CDKN1B, looks like MEN1 and is the diagnosis to consider when menin sequencing is negative. Familial medullary thyroid carcinoma without other MEN2 features is also RET-related.

von Hippel-Lindau disease causes pheochromocytoma or paraganglioma, clear-cell renal carcinoma, hemangioblastoma, and pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors or cysts. It is a VHL variant on chromosome 3. Screen the kidneys and the central nervous system, not only the adrenals.

Carney complex, often PRKAR1A, includes spotty pigmentation, cardiac myxoma, primary pigmented nodular adrenocortical disease causing ACTH-independent Cushing syndrome, and growth hormone excess. An echocardiogram is part of care because the myxoma can embolize.

Hyperparathyroidism-jaw tumor syndrome, from CDC73, carries a high risk of parathyroid carcinoma, ossifying fibromas of the jaw, and renal and uterine lesions. A palpable parathyroid mass or a very high PTH in a young patient should raise this diagnosis before a routine adenoma is assumed.

Genetic testing is done before thyroidectomy when medullary carcinoma is diagnosed, because a positive RET result changes the operation and forces a pheochromocytoma screen in the patient and the family. Do not operate first and counsel later.

topics.title: Gastroenteropancreatic neuroendocrine tumours
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 43 Neuroendocrine Tumors and Disorders

mustKnow.fact: Insulinoma causes fasting hypoglycemia with endogenous hyperinsulinism and is usually a small benign intrapancreatic tumor. About 10% are malignant and about 10% occur in MEN1. Localize only after the biochemical diagnosis, with multiphase CT or endoscopic ultrasound. Diazoxide is used when the tumor cannot be removed.

Gastrinoma causes Zollinger-Ellison syndrome: severe peptic ulcer disease beyond the duodenal bulb, diarrhea, and a high gastrin that rises paradoxically after secretin. Many tumors lie in the gastrinoma triangle. About a quarter are part of MEN1. Stop a proton pump inhibitor only with a plan, because it raises gastrin and because ulcer perforation is the risk.

Glucagonoma causes diabetes, weight loss, venous thrombosis, and necrolytic migratory erythema, usually from a tumor in the pancreatic tail. VIPoma causes watery diarrhea, hypokalemia, and acidosis (WDHA). Somatostatinoma is rare and classically combines diabetes, gallstones, and steatorrhea.

Carcinoid syndrome, flushing and secretory diarrhea with right-sided heart-valve fibrosis, occurs when a midgut neuroendocrine tumor has liver metastases, so serotonin reaches the systemic circulation. Measure 24-hour urinary 5-HIAA. Niacin deficiency can occur because tryptophan is consumed to make serotonin.

Give octreotide before an invasive procedure in a patient with carcinoid syndrome to reduce the risk of carcinoid crisis. A long-acting somatostatin analogue is also first-line control of the syndrome. Telotristat can be added for diarrhea that escapes a somatostatin analogue.

WHO grading uses Ki-67. Grade 1 is below 3%, grade 2 is 3% to 20%, and grade 3 is above 20%. A well-differentiated grade 3 neuroendocrine tumor is not the same disease as a poorly differentiated neuroendocrine carcinoma, which is treated more like a small-cell cancer.

Ga-68 DOTATATE PET is the imaging test for well-differentiated tumors that express somatostatin receptors. FDG PET is more useful when the tumor is high grade and receptor negative. Choose the scan from the grade, not by habit.

Peptide receptor radionuclide therapy with Lu-177 DOTATATE improved progression-free survival in midgut neuroendocrine tumors in NETTER-1. Everolimus and sunitinib are systemic options for progressive pancreatic neuroendocrine tumors. Surgery is still the only cure for a localized tumor.

topics.title: Autoimmune polyglandular syndromes and immunotherapy endocrinopathies
topics.book: Williams Textbook of Endocrinology 15e Ch. 44 The Immunoendocrinopathy Syndromes

mustKnow.fact: Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 1, APECED, is autosomal recessive AIRE deficiency. The classic triad is chronic mucocutaneous candidiasis, hypoparathyroidism, and Addison disease. Two of the three make the clinical diagnosis. It begins in childhood.

Autoimmune polyendocrine syndrome type 2 is Addison disease plus autoimmune thyroid disease (Schmidt syndrome), with or without type 1 diabetes (Carpenter syndrome). It is polygenic, HLA-related, and presents in adults. Candidiasis and hypoparathyroidism are not part of it, which separates it from APS-1.

IPEX syndrome is FOXP3 dysfunction in boys: infancy-onset diabetes, severe enteropathy, and eczema. It is not APS-1. Hematopoietic transplant is the disease-directed treatment, and insulin alone does not fix the enteropathy.

CTLA-4 blockade, such as ipilimumab, is the checkpoint inhibitor most likely to cause hypophysitis, often with permanent ACTH deficiency. PD-1 and PD-L1 blockade more often cause thyroiditis, which is thyrotoxic and then permanently hypothyroid.

Checkpoint inhibitor-induced diabetes presents as insulin-deficient diabetes, often in diabetic ketoacidosis, sometimes with GAD antibodies, and it is usually permanent. Do not treat it as ordinary type 2 diabetes with metformin.

Primary adrenal insufficiency from immunotherapy is uncommon but life-threatening. A tired, hypotensive patient on a PD-1 inhibitor needs a cortisol before the fatigue is blamed on the cancer. Give hydrocortisone if the patient is unstable, and do not wait for the ACTH result.

High-dose glucocorticoid for hypophysitis reduces mass effect and headache but rarely restores ACTH secretion. Thyroid hormone is replaced in the hypothyroid phase of thyroiditis and is not stopped just because the immunotherapy is continued. Endocrine adverse effects usually do not require stopping a drug that is controlling the cancer.
mustKnow.source: ASCO endocrine irAE guidance; Williams Endocrinology 15e Ch. 44

mustKnow.fact: HIV can cause euthyroid sick physiology, opportunistic adrenalitis including tuberculosis and CMV, and lipodystrophy from older antiretrovirals. A low cortisol in advanced HIV is adrenal insufficiency until proved otherwise, not a routine sick-euthyroid result.
